title: Give a care recipient a usable voice and an independent help route

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A care handover must preserve the recipient’s communication, preferences and essential agreed needs. An independent concern route must be accessible and genuinely separate from the person involved; it is not a promise of absolute secrecy.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional flawed handover: “Visitor at 14:00; helper will answer; afternoon water setup probably done.” Recipient uses a communication device, wants 13:30 or no visit, and wants a private concern heard. Existing care plan requires an accessible water cup set out at 13:00; this is ordinary setup, not a new clinical instruction. Backup worker is on duty and authorized to confirm setup. Independent service advocate accepts device-supported text at 13:15; if unavailable, a separate duty supervisor accepts the same mode. Neither is implicated in the concern.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Rewrite the handover with confirmed/pending states, recipient-led communication and an immediate check of the agreed missed setup. Draft the private route without investigating or diagnosing neglect.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: The only suggested complaint contact is the helper whose conduct is questioned. Is writing the number enough for an independent route?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Use the recipient’s chosen visit preference and let them answer with their device. Ask the authorized worker to verify/carry out the existing setup promptly; “probably” is not confirmation. Later fiction: worker confirms setup 13:05; advocate appointment is requested, not held. Partial: provide a complaint route while leaving the current need unaddressed. Incorrect: let the helper answer instead or promise secrecy regardless of actual duties.
criteria: Recipient choice and communication are preserved
Current needs and independent concerns have distinct routes
Pending and confirmed actions are not conflated

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Identify an appropriate genuinely separate service route and a usable communication mode; immediate danger needs local emergency assistance. Do not require confrontation with someone controlling essential support.
